name: Tokoloshe, Mythic
body:
MYTHIC TOKOLOSHE
CR 4/1

The water churns and splashes as a small, stocky humanoid surges forth, gnashing rows of needle-like teeth, its eye sockets merely deep gouges. As if it were one with the water itself, it darts quickly forward, shouting curses and swinging its fists.

XP 800
CE Small undead (aquatic, mythic)
Init +2; Senses blindsense 60 ft., blindsight 30 ft.; Perception +12

DEFENSE

AC 16, touch 13, flat-footed 14 (+2 Dex, +3 natural, +1 size)
hp 34 (4d8+16)
Fort +2, Ref +3, Will +6
Defensive Abilities channel resistance +2, water diffusionma; DR 5/slashing; Immune undead traits; Resist fire 10
Weaknesses blind

OFFENSE

Speed 20 ft., swim 30 ft., waverider
Melee bite +6 (1d4+2), 2 slams +6 (1d3+2)
Special Attacks mythic power (3/day, surge ++1d6), trickster’s torment
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 4th; concentration +5)

3/day—invisibility

STATISTICS

Str 4, Dex 15, Con —, Int 8, Wis 15, Cha 13
Base Atk +3; CMB +4; CMD 16
Feats Extra Mythic Power, Skill Focus (Perception), Toughness
Skills Climb +9, Perception +12, Stealth +13, Swim +10
Languages Common, Polyglot

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Blind

A tikoloshe has no eyes and is blind. All creatures beyond the range of its hearing-based blindsense and blindsight abilities have total concealment against it.

Trickster’s Torment (Su)

The tikoloshe makes a melee touch attack against a living creature, affecting it as bestow curse (DC 15 Will negates) for 24 hours. It can use this ability once per day but can use it again by expending one use of mythic power each time.

It can instead spend one use of mythic power to make the effect permanent. A creature can only suffer from one tikoloshe’s curse at a time. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Water Diffusion (Ex)

When in water at least 2 feet deep, a tikoloshe’s body seems to diffuse into and become part of the water, granting it concealment (20% miss chance) as if under the effect of blur. This effect ends immediately upon entering shallower water or setting foot on land. It can expend one use of mythic power as a swift action to gain displacement as long as it remains in deeper water, or to maintain its blur in shallow water or even on land as long as it is within 10 feet of water. This enhanced effect lasts for 1d4+1 rounds.

Waverider (Ex)

Up to 3 times per day, a tikoloshe can swim up to 30 feet as a swift action. It does not provoke an attack of opportunity for this movement.

ECOLOGY

Environment warm forests, oceans, or rivers
Organization solitary, gang (2-8), or clan (9-20)
Treasure standard

Cruel and spiteful, tokoloshe (singular and plural; also called tikoloshe) are small undead that haunt tropical waterways and jungles, preying on travelers and villagers alike with their magical abilities and appetite for harm. Tokoloshe stand no higher than a gnome or a human child, but their bodies are dense and muscular; many have large potbellies and arms long enough for their knuckles to score the dirt as they walk. Their creation leaves them with blackened, eyeless sockets, but tokoloshe can “see” using their giant, bat-like ears. Their skin is smooth and shines whether wet or dry.

Tokoloshe are genderless; they stand about 4 feet tall and weigh almost 150 pounds.

Depending on the ritual used and the quality of the materials, some tokoloshe look different than the standard dwarf-gremlin variety. Some look like horrid beast-headed humanoids or as a worm-like creature with a dog’s head and golden tongue. These variants may or may not have the burned-out eyeholes of the “standard” tokoloshe.
